Ostrava-Lune Foundation, Halbrecht Early Inquiry Grants: eligibility rules (2027 cycle)
An application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. The project period, from start date to end date, may not exceed 39 weeks.
R2. Applications hosted by a teaching hospital may budget at most $5,000 for travel.
R3. The lead applicant must have received a doctorate no more than 6 years before 2027. This rule does not apply if the applicant has a documented Corran career break and the doctorate is at most 10 years old.
R4. The application must include a letter of support from the host. This rule does not apply if the host is a university, whose standing agreement with the foundation replaces the letter.
R5. If the type of host institution is not stated, treat the host as an independent institute.
R6. Research with human participants requires approval from the Mereth ethics board.
R7. If ethics approval is not mentioned, assume none was obtained.
R8. Equipment and travel together may not exceed $30,000.
R9. The host institution must be a university, a teaching hospital or a community laboratory.

According to the CV, the lead applicant was awarded a doctorate in 2024. The title of the project was shortened at the suggestion of the host's grants office. The host did not provide a letter of support. Equipment purchases are budgeted at $30,000. The budget sheet asks the foundation for 40 thousand dollars in total. Only soil and water samples are studied, with no human participants. Several figures in the narrative were drawn by a graduate student. Travel is budgeted at $0. The applicant has not applied to the Mereth ethics board. The cover letter thanks two former mentors by name. The project is scheduled to begin on January 4, 2027. The host institution is a university. That makes a project period of 34 weeks. The team expects to wrap up on August 30, 2027. Equipment and travel together come to $30,000. The team commits, in an attached plan, to releasing all data openly.

R3. Participants on an anticoagulant must have a resting heart rate of at most 85 beats per minute.
R4. Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 14 days after it.
R5. Participants taking an anticoagulant are excluded, unless they enroll at a tier A Halvard site, where coagulation is monitored weekly.
R6. The Kelman fibrosis index may not exceed 10.
R7. Participants must be between 25 and 75 years old inclusive.
R8. Tier C Halvard sites may only enroll participants aged 45 or younger.
R9. If the site tier is not recorded, treat the site as tier B.
